title: The Dawn Patrol
byline: Howard Hawks's 1930 WWI aviation drama from First National Pictures (Vitaphone), starring Richard Barthelmess and Douglas Fairbanks Jr.; originally released as 'Flight Commander.'

editorial:
Howard Hawks's debut as a solo director on a major studio production, The Dawn Patrol (released under the title Flight Commander) is a 1930 First Nationalâ€“Vitaphone sound film set in the Royal Flying Corps on the Western Front in 1915. Richard Barthelmess plays Courtney, a combat squadron commander buried under orders from a distant, indifferent high command that funnels barely-trained replacements into morning patrols with near-zero survival rates; Douglas Fairbanks Jr. is his closest friend Scott. Hawks shot real aerial footage and flew an uncredited cameo as a German pilot. The film's anti-war bitterness is unusually direct for a 1930 prestige production, and the Vitaphone sound designâ€”engines, gunfire, the drone of approaching formationsâ€”was technically ambitious for the transitional era. Filmmakers and archivists working on WWI aviation, early-sound-cinema craft, or pre-Code Hollywood will find the footage freely usable: no renewal was filed for 'The Dawn Patrol' or its alternate title 'Flight Commander' in the Catalog of Copyright Entries 1957â€“1959, and the print is in the public domain.

The one rights trap is the Warner Archive transfer. Warner Bros., inheriting the First National catalog through United Artists and Turner, distributes the film commercially on disc and may assert rights in its specific transfer. Any copy sourced from the Warner Archive DVD/Blu-ray could carry thin new authorship in the color grading or redrawn title cards WB commissioned. The Archive.org copy (identifier FlightCommander1930AkaTheDawnPatrolDouglasFairbanksJrHowardHawks, uploaded 2014) predates that transfer and carries no license restrictionâ€”use it as your starting point. Also note that no print with authentic original title cards is known to survive: when WB acquired the catalog they discarded the original frames, and all extant prints feature replacement titles drawn after the fact.
faq: Is The Dawn Patrol (1930) in the public domain, or does Warner Bros. own it?

The underlying film is in the public domain. No copyright renewal was found for 'The Dawn Patrol' or its original release title 'Flight Commander' in the Catalog of Copyright Entries for 1957â€“1959, and the 95-year maximum term would have expired January 1, 2026 in any case. Warner Bros. distributes the film via Warner Archive and may claim rights in their specific transfer, but the 1930 film itself belongs to no one. Use the Archive.org copy to avoid any dispute over the WB transfer.
The film was based on a short story â€” do I need to clear rights to that story separately?

No. John Monk Saunders's original story 'The Flight Commander' was created for the film and published no later than 1930. All US works published through 1930 are in the public domain by term, so the source material requires no separate clearance.
